title: Later Liang
capsule: The Later Liang was one of the Sixteen Kingdoms founded in 386 by Lü Guang of the Di people in the Hexi Corridor (modern Gansu), centered on Guzang (present-day Wuwei). Lü Guang had been a general of the Former Qin and returned westward with Central Asian booty—including the Buddhist monk Kumārajīva—after the Battle of Fei River (383) broke Former Qin power. The state was notable as the location where Kumārajīva spent years before being taken to Chang'an in 401, profoundly shaping Chinese Buddhist translation. Later Liang fragmented rapidly under Lü Guang's successors, and was conquered by the Later Qin under Yao Xing in 403.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Later Liang's core territory in the Hexi Corridor is well established; exact frontiers against contemporaneous Sixteen Kingdoms states are uncertain.
